# WatermarkOut

> A free, open-source watermark remover for AI-generated images and short videos.
> The AI model runs entirely inside the user's browser via WebAssembly, so files
> are never uploaded to any server. There is no backend, no account system and no
> telemetry.

WatermarkOut removes watermarks and small unwanted objects by inpainting: the user
masks a region and a GAN fills it in from the surrounding pixels. Pixels outside the
mask are copied through unchanged.

## Key facts

- **Cost:** free, with no paid tier. There is no server to pay for, so there is nothing to meter.
- **Privacy:** images and videos never leave the browser tab. The only network requests are the app's own static files and a one-time 29 MB model download from Hugging Face on first visit. The model is checksum-verified and cached locally.
- **Model:** MI-GAN (Picsart Research, ICCV 2023), run through ONNX Runtime Web with a WebGPU → WASM fallback chain.
- **Output:** no watermark is added to results. Save as PNG, JPG or WebP.
- **Offline:** works fully offline after the first visit; installable as a PWA.
- **Licence:** MIT. Source at https://github.com/IamRamgarhia/free-ai-watermark-remover
- **Author:** Prince Ramgarhia (DiceCodes), Batala, Punjab, India.

## Supported watermarks

Detection is structural rather than a table of known logos, so it is not limited to
a fixed list. Which generators actually stamp a visible badge, as of August 2026:

- Google Gemini / Imagen — yes, bottom-right. Paid tiers can now disable it at source.
- Grok (xAI) — yes, but xAI's Acceptable Use Policy prohibits removing it.
- Bing Image Creator / Designer — yes, bottom-left (last confirmed 2024).
- Meta AI — older images only; newer Meta models watermark invisibly instead.
- Midjourney — NO. Midjourney has never added a visible watermark on any tier.
- OpenAI / DALL·E — NO. DALL·E 2 and 3 were retired in May 2026.
- Adobe Firefly — unclear; reports conflict.

## What removal does not do

Removing a visible badge does not make an image undetectable as AI-generated.
Google's SynthID (also present on OpenAI images) and Meta's Content Seal are encoded
across the whole image, not stamped in a corner, and survive cropping, resizing,
re-compression, screenshots and AI upscaling. Saving from this tool does strip the
file's C2PA Content Credentials metadata, but that is an unavoidable side effect of
how browsers export images and does not affect the pixel-level watermark.

## Supported formats

- Images: JPG, PNG, WebP, BMP — up to about 100 MB
- Video: MP4, WebM, MOV — short clips, audio preserved
- Browsers: Chrome/Edge 90+, Firefox 90+, Safari 16.4+

## Known limitations

- Busy backgrounds (faces, fine text, brickwork) reconstruct poorly — this is a
  limitation of inpainting models generally, not a defect.
- Video uses a single static patch applied across frames, so it suits fixed corner
  watermarks; a watermark that moves is not handled.
- Long videos are slow because every frame is decoded and re-encoded in the browser.
- The model reconstructs plausible pixels; it does not recover what was underneath.

## Intended use

For images the user created or otherwise has the right to edit. Not intended for
stripping watermarks from other people's copyrighted work, circumventing stock
licensing, or passing AI-generated images off as photographs.
